title: Kernel-aware prefill scheduler and attention hook for speculative decode fastpath and safe fallback
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Background: We need a prefill/decode orchestration layer that is aware of target kernel capabilities (memory/occupancy/optimized attention kernels) and can route speculative decode requests to a fastpath when the kernel and attention footprint align. When the fastpath cannot guarantee output quality or SLOs, the runtime must gracefully fallback to a conservative path without causing large latency spikes or token duplication.

Goal: Implement a kernel-aware prefill scheduler plus a lightweight attention-hint hook that: (1) scores candidate kernels per-request by expected memory and compute fit, (2) schedules prefill windows to maximize reuse (KV cache-friendly grouping), (3) injects attention metadata so model runtimes can pick optimized attention kernels, and (4) defines deterministic fallback/runback strategies triggered by acceptance metrics.

Scope: Prototype scheduler and attention hook in the runtime agent and a toggled path for speculative decode fastpath. Include telemetry, rollout plan (canary), and runbook for fallback. This ticket covers design, a PoC implementation, integration test harness, and a canary rollout. The full rollout and perf tuning will be subsequent work.

Non-goals: Full multi-tenant autoscaler changes, model re-training, or changing model checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can produce a kernel-fit score for each incoming request in <= 2ms median overhead
When fastpath conditions are met, >= 85% of speculative-prefill requests are routed to fastpath without increasing observed 95th pct latency by > 10%
Fallback is triggered deterministically when acceptance_confidence < 0.65 or kernel-oom risk > 0.9, and fallback completes with rollback_latency < 40ms median
No measurable regression in token-level quality for production prompt set (quality_regression < 1% on eval set tied to release) when canaried on 1% traffic
Telemetry exposes metrics: runtime.kernel_fit_score, runtime.attention_hint_triggered, runtime.spec_acceptance_rate, runtime.fallback_count, runtime.rollback_latency_ms
Canary rollout document and runbook exist and were reviewed by SRE and Support
Unit and integration tests covering kernel scoring logic and fallback paths are in CI and passing
tasks: Design kernel-fit scoring function (weights for memory, compute, attention_type, sequence_length) - draft doc
Add attention-hint header in prefill RPC and semantics for supported attention opt modes
Implement prefill scheduler hook that computes fit score and selects kernel target
Implement safe fallback: abort fastpath decode, requeue prefill on conservative kernel, commit acceptance decision
Add telemetry events and dashboard panels for acceptance metrics and fallback rates
Integration tests: simulate kernel OOM, degraded kernel throughput, and acceptance false positives
Canary rollout plan and runbook with rollback criteria
